title: AI is becoming a disaster for the climate
lede: Brian Merchant's Blood in the Machine essay draws on two recent studies of AI's carbon footprint and singles out Anthropic's turn to natural gas for its data centers.

points: A Harvard-led study of 403 large US data centers found 54% of their power came from fossil fuels, about 25.7 million tonnes of CO2 a year.
Citing HEATED, Merchant calls that a floor: it misses on-site gas turbines such as xAI's Colossus, refrigerant leaks and methane losses.
Ketan Joshi's State of AI Climate Impact 2026 report says AI may already rival international aviation over its lifecycle.
Joshi notes Anthropic has never disclosed emissions data and recently bought 1.7 GW of gas generators in a $3.4bn deal.
The essay also attacks the BAAJA permitting bill, which passed the Senate, for weakening local tools to fight data centers.

points.text: The leading pushback sets the cited 20 megatons against about 6,200 from animal agriculture and says the climate case falls flat.
Even a self-described harsh AI critic faults the essay for leaving out baselines such as emissions from existing cloud data centers.
One commenter says AI at least has a chance of helping reverse climate change; a reply flatly rejects that.
Others want data centers to disclose their energy use whatever one thinks of them, and point to Spain's 80% renewables mandate.
